requirement: In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference, inline or fenced, MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. A fenced reference MUST render its badge followed by its body as Markdown. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. A badge link MUST show a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and MAY brighten on hover. Badges MAY be laid out inline with the surrounding text, a fenced reference's badge and body MAY be visually set apart from the surrounding text as one block, and a built-in's unlinked badge MAY show a help cursor to signal its hover text. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.targets`.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** I read the code marked {impl} and the tests marked {test}, and found no unmarked implementation and no unspecified behavior in the marked code.

**Implementation**
- **Badge image.** `shield_badge` (src/lib.rs) builds a Shields.io static badge. Its `alt` is "role full-name", for example `cite rules.other`. `ReferenceKind::label` and `color` supply the role and color. `DefinitionKind::badge` supplies the definition kind (`req` or `example`).
- **Inline and fenced references.** `reference_badge` turns a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference into a link to the badge at the definition. The link target is `chapter_href` with the anchor from `DefinitionKind::anchor`.
  - `chapter_href` produces relative links, including `../` from nested chapters.
  - A built-in name becomes an unlinked `<span class="… habeas-builtin" title=…>` whose hover text is the built-in's text.
  - An unknown name, an invalid form, or a `{term}` target returns `None`, so the text stays literal.
  - `replace_inline_references` handles inline roles.
  - `replace_references` uses `fenced::markdown_fences` (`MarkdownFence`, `markdown_fences`). It emits the badge followed by the body, and the body is processed recursively as Markdown.
  - An unclosed fence and fences inside code blocks or raw HTML stay literal.
- **Definition badges.** `replace_definitions` renders each valid, closed `{req}` or `{example}` directive as a definition badge. The badge is an element with `id="habeas-<kind>-<name>"`, which is what the reference links target. Invalid names, unclosed directives, and directives inside code stay literal.
- **Stylesheet.** `md/habeas.css` carries the visual obligations.
  - Visited links keep `color: inherit`, the same as unvisited links.
  - `:focus-visible` draws a 2px outline.
  - `:hover` only applies `brightness(1.08)`.
  - `.habeas-builtin` gets `cursor: help`.
  - `.habeas-fenced-ref` sets the block apart.
- **Marking.** `preprocess_book` only orchestrates these functions, so it does not need a book_badges {impl}. The extra behavior in the marked functions (the "See evidence" link, `term` labels, `%2Emd` escaping) carries its own {impl} markers for other definitions, such as index.navigation and definitions.references.

**Tests**
- `fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked` covers the fenced reference cases:
  - The badge link is followed by the Markdown body.
  - The fence markers are removed.
  - A fenced reference nested in a requirement works.
  - A built-in renders as an unlinked badge with hover text.
  - An inline role with escaped wording stays literal.
  - An unknown name stays literal.
  - A fenced reference inside a code block stays literal.
- `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` checks `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` links, colors, and image URLs from `guides/deep.md` to `../requirements.html#…`.
- `examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them` covers example definition badges (alt text and anchor), cross-chapter links to an example, and literal handling of invalid and code-block directives.
- `shields_badge_urls_escape_requirement_names` covers Shields.io URL escaping and the alt text.
- `colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal` checks that text outside a directive stays literal and that definition bodies render as Markdown.
- `badge_stylesheet_keeps_visited_links_legible_and_shows_focus` covers the stylesheet:
  - Visited declarations equal unvisited ones.
  - A visible focus outline exists.
  - Hover only brightens.
  - Only Habeas selectors are styled.

The tests cover the interesting boundaries and failure cases. The only untested optional items are the `cursor: help` and block-layout styling, which the requirement marks as MAY.

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references: discovery MUST skip `.git` and `target` directories at any depth and the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories.
